test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 27 Nov, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
When there are two parallel lines cut by a transversal, which of the following is true?

a) Corresponding angles are equal.

b) Alternate interior angles are supplementary.

c) Consecutive angles on the same side of the transversal are equal.

d) Alternate interior angles are equal?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In **geometry**, when two **parallel lines** are intersected by a **transversal**:

• **Corresponding angles** are always **equal** (Statement a is true).

• **Alternate interior angles** are always **equal** (Statement d is true, statement b is false).

• **Consecutive (co-interior) angles** sum to 180°, meaning they are **supplementary**, not equal (Statement c is false).

**∴ The correct answer is a and d .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two parallel lines (m || n) and a transversal line (t).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/237ad79d0ea437bd360bb8c22a6cbd7af855e3a9118f9550b59c60ec1dfb2f52.png] 

Analyzing the pairs of angles from the diagram:

⇒ **Corresponding Angles:** Pairs like ∠1 and ∠5 or ∠2 and ∠6 are in the same relative position. By the **Corresponding Angles Postulate**, ∠1 = ∠5. Hence, statement (a) is **true**.

⇒ **Alternate Interior Angles:** Pairs like ∠4 and ∠6 or ∠3 and ∠5 are on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines. By the **Alternate Interior Angles Theorem**, ∠4 = ∠6. Hence, statement (d) is **true**.

⇒ **Alternate Interior Angles (Supplementary check):** Since ∠4 = ∠6, they are only supplementary if they are both 90°. In general, they are **equal**, not supplementary. Hence, statement (b) is **false**.

⇒ **Consecutive Interior Angles:** Pairs like ∠4 and ∠5 are on the same side. By the **Consecutive Interior Angles Theorem**, ∠4 + ∠5 = 180°. They are **supplementary**, not necessarily equal. Hence, statement (c) is **false**.

**∴ The correct answer is a and d .**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite each other at the vertex are always equal (e.g., ∠1 = ∠3 and ∠2 = ∠4).

Linear Pair of Angles

Angles that lie on a straight line and share a common arm are supplementary, meaning their sum is 180° (e.g., ∠1 + ∠2 = 180°).

Alternate Exterior Angles

Pairs of angles on opposite sides of the transversal and outside the parallel lines (e.g., ∠1 and ∠7) are always equal.</p
